newsitem.title: CANADA: StatsCan June wheat seeding estimate up from April.
newsitem.headline: StatsCan June wheat seeding estimate up from April.

text.p: Statistics Canada in its June planting intentions report said that Canadian farmers would plant 28.2 million acres of wheat, down slightly from its April estimate of 28.8 million acres.
The 1997 all wheat number is 8.1 percent lower than total wheat plantings of 30.7 million acres in 1996 in Canada, the federal statistics agency said.
Statistics Canada released the following data based on a survey done between May 26 and June 4.

Statistics Canada said cold and wet weather delayed seeding across most of the agricultural areas of Canada during May, but warmer conditions at the end of May allowed farmers to accelerate their seeding plans.
The agency said that by the end of the first week of June, half of the farmers responding to its survey in the Prairie provinces reported that seeding was at least 95 percent completed.
StatsCan's satellite imagery of the Red River Valley in Manitoba showed that about 450,000 acres were initially flooded this spring, but only 5,000 acres in that area were not seeded as of June 14.

Statistics Canada said that weaker world wheat prices partially explain farmers' intentions to plant 2.6 million fewer acres of spring wheat this crop year compared to last year, a drop of 10.4 percent.
Durum wheat acreage increased 8.1 percent on the year, partly because of renewed interest in Canadian durum from international markets and expected higher prices, StatsCan said.

A rise of 38.4 percent on the year in canola seedings to 12.1 million acres does not approach the record set in 1994 at 14.3 million acres, but it does reverse the downward trend that has occurred since then, the agency said.
StatsCan said that its satellite data of crop development as of June 23 showed yield expectations are down in Manitoba and Saskatchewan but up in Alberta.
